Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Vivek Jain

Misc. Appeal No. 1016 of 2014
 National Insurance Company
 Versus
 Smt. Laxmi Bai And Others

.............................................................
 Appearance:
 Ms. Amrit Kaur Ruprah-Advocate for the appellant.
Shri A.S. Parihar - Advocate for the respondents.

Ms. Amrit Kaur Ruprah-Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri A.S. Parihar - Advocate for the respondents.
(Reserved on 05.02.2025) (Pronounced on 10. 02.2024)

The present appeals are filed by the insurance company arising out of common award dated 27.01.2014 passed by Additional MACT,
Maihar, District Satna in C.T. Nos. 98/2012 and 102/2012.
C.T. No. 98/2012 was filed arising out of death of Rajesh Patel in the accident and from which M.A. No. 1016/2014 has arisen.

C.T.
No.102/2012 was filed arising out of injuries caused to injured Anup Singh in the same accident and arising from which M.A. No. 1017/2014 has been filed.

2. The learned counsel for the appellant-insurance company in both the appeals submits that there is false implication of the vehicle and that nothing has been placed on record by way of evidence by the claimants in the claim case that the jeep insured by the appellant company was involved in the accident.

3. The facts in brief are that the claimants alleged that on 28.08.2012 deceased Rajesh Patel and National Insurance Company vs Smt. Laxmi Bai on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19854527/
1 injured Anup Singh were riding motorcycle No.MP-21MD-0857 and were going from village Dhanwahi to M/s. KJS Cement Factory Maihar, District Satna.

entities.text: National Insurance Company vs Smt. Laxmi Bai
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When they reached near Dadu Dhaba then the Commander Jeep No. MP-19F-2259 being driving rashly and negligently by respondent-Pradeep Kumar and owned by respondent Rajendra Prasad, dashed the motorcycle as a result of which both the persons fell down.

Deceased Rajesh Patel expired while on the way to hospital while the injured Anup Singh was given primary treatment at Civil Hospital, Maihar where he remained admitted for two days, thereafter he got himself treated at Nahar Nursingh Home,
Satna by private Doctors and in C.T. Scan he was found to have suffered fracture in skull and remained under treatment.
4. The claim was defended by the insurance company on the ground that the income of the deceased and injured is not as is claimed in the claim petitions.

It was further contended that the implication of the vehicle (jeep) insured by the appellant company is not made out in the accident and no death was caused to deceased Rajesh Patel no injuries caused to Anup Singh by any accident caused by the said jeep.
The Claims Tribunal after considering the rival pleadings so also the evidence adduced before it has awarded both the claim petitions.

C.T.No.98/2012 has been awarded to the tune of Rs.19,25,000/- and C.T. No.102/2012 has been awarded Rs.41,700/-.
5.

The learned counsel for the appellant while taking this Court through the evidence adduced before the Claims Tribunal has contended that the implication of jeep is not made out from the record and from evidence adduced before the Tribunal.

It was vehemently argued that there is only one eyewitness to the incident who is injured Anup Singh and was one of the two persons travelling on the motorcycle, the other one i.e. Rajesh Patel having expired in the accident.

6. The learned counsel for the appellant-company has vehemently argued that looking to paragraph-8 of deposition of Anup Singh (AW-2) there is no possibility that he could have seen the Jeep in the manner accident is described by him.

It is argued that as per deposition of Anup Singh (AW-2) the jeep dashed the motorcycle from behind and AW-2 has admitted that before the accident both the persons could not see the jeep prior in time and further admitted that the jeep did not stop at the place of accident and therefore, there is no reason how this injured witness AW-2 could have seen the jeep and could have noted down the jeep number.
Thus, it is a clear case of false implication.

7. It was further argued by learned counsel for the appellant company that the date of accident as alleged is 28.08.2012 whereas the FIR has been lodged on 10.10.2012 and looking to so much delay in lodging the FIR i.e. almost 1 month and 12 days, it is highly likely that vehicle has been roped in at a later stage and as an afterthought.
Heavy reliance is made on delayed lodgment of the FIR.
8. On the question of quantum also it is argued that the quantum as assessed by the Tribunal is at higher side.

9. Per contra, it is argued by learned counsel for the claimants that there was no delay in lodging of the FIR given the fact that one of the two persons had expired in the accident and other was injured having suffered fracture in frontal bone of skull.

It is further argued that the mere delay in lodging of National Insurance Company vs Smt. Laxmi Bai on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19854527/
2 the FIR in the given Indian conditions cannot be held to be fatal to the case of claimants and further that other injured person i.e. Anup Singh (AW-2) since remained admitted at Maihar Hospital for primary treatment and thereafter was treated as Satna by private Doctors and underwent C.T. Scan etc, the delay in lodging the FIR cannot be held to be fatal.

entities.text: National Insurance Company vs Smt. Laxmi Bai
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further argued that looking to the entire deposition of Anup Singh (AW-2), it inspires confidence in truthfulness of his deposition.

10. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
11.
So far as the question of delayed lodgement of the FIR is concerned, this Court has gone through the FIR in question which is part of the record of the Claims Tribunal as Ex.P-2.
The FIR though is lodged on 10.10.2012 but in the column of receipt of information at the police station, the date is clearly mentioned as 04.09.2011 at 8:20 in the evening.
The FIR mentions that the same has been registered after the merg enquiry.

The delay of 1 month and 12 days as projected by counsel for the appellant is not made out looking to the bare perusal of the FIR (Ex.P-2) which categorically mentions that information was received at police station on 04.09.2012 which is within seven days of occurrence of accident.
Merely because due to pendency of merg enquiry formal lodgment of FIR was delayed, would not make the entire case doubtful.

12. The Supreme Court in the case of Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan and Ors. (2011) 4 SCC 693 has held that mere delay in lodging the FIR cannot be a valid ground to doubt the claimant's case in genuine cases.

entities.text: Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan and Ors. (2011) 4 SCC 693
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is held that in Indian conditions, it is not expected that a person would rush to police station after the incident, and that treatment of victim is given priority over lodging of FIR and the relatives of victim are not expected to mechanically lodge FIR with promptitude immediately after accident.

In the aforesaid case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held as under:-
"17.
It is well settled that delay in lodging the FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the police station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the police station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the police.

Delay in lodging the FIR thus,
cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
18. In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinised more carefully.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.

19. Lodging of FIR certainly proves the factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for National Insurance Company vs Smt. Laxmi Bai on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19854527/
3 rejecting the claim petition.

entities.text: National Insurance Company vs Smt. Laxmi Bai
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be a variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgement of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquillity of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons."

13. In the instant case not only information was first given to the police station within 7 days of the accident but these circumstances are also important to note that one of the victims of accident had died on the way to hospital on the same day and other victim i.e. injured Anup Singh (AW-2) was himself admitted at Maihar Hospital for two days which is duly established by discharge ticket available on record as Ex.P-16.

The other treatment papers placed on record as Ex.P-17, P-18 and P-19 establish that the said injured person suffered fracture of frontal bone and C.T. Scan report is placed on record as Ex.P-14 dated 30.08.2012.

Thus, it can be safely said that the injured was in need of immediate treatment and was receiving treatment immediately after accident and therefore,
mere 7 days delay in giving intimation to police station cannot be held to be fatal in the present case.
14.

The counsel for the appellant had also argued that looking to the deposition of Anup Singh (AW-2) there is no possibility that he could have seen the accident in the manner it is stated to have occurred.
This Court has gone through the deposition of Anup Singh (AW-2).

In para-8 of his deposition he has mentioned that it is true that they could not see the jeep prior to accident and explained that the jeep hit them from behind and because the jeep hit them from behind he could not see that how the jeep was being driven and further said that the jeep did not stop at the spot after hitting them but this was stated in response to a suggestion given by counsel for the insurance company and in the very next sentence, he on his own volition stated that after about 200-250 meter the jeep driver stopped the jeep.

Thus, this Court does not find substance in the argument of learned counsel for the appellant that since the jeep hit the motorcycle from behind there is no possibility that injured Anup Singh could have seen the jeep or could have noted the jeep number.
The injured Anup Singh has himself stated in para-8 that the jeep driver stopped the jeep after 200-250 meters.
Anup Singh (AW-2) though was injured but in para-9 of his deposition has further stated that after the accident he stood up himself and called out for help.
Thus, it cannot be said that Anup Singh (AW-2) could not have seen the accident or could not have noted down the jeep number.
15. As per discharge ticket, he was admitted on 29.08.2012 in Civil Hospital Maihar and discharged on 30.08.2012 and advised C.T. Scan of head and ENT opinion.
The C.T. Scan report and ENT opinion are on record which are dated 30.08.2012.
Thus, the entire treatment of injured Anup Singh (AW-2) is connected and related to what has been mentioned in the discharge ticket of Civil Hospital, Maihar.

4 16.

sentences.text: In view of the above, this Court does not find any fact in the case to accept the proposition put up by appellant-insurance company that there is false implication of the offending vehicle insured with the appellant- insurance company.
17. Coming to the question of quantum of compensation, the learned counsel for the appellant had vehemently argued that the quantum has been assessed by the Claims Tribunal at the higher side.

However, the counsel for the appellant could not dispute the position at the time of argument that the quantum which has been assessed has been assessed by the Tribunal prior to the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 and if future prospects are calculated then even accepting the argument of appellant in the matter of income and dependency, the quantum would not change.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18. In view of the above, this Court finds no reason to interfere in the impugned award passed by the Claims Tribunal.
Appeals being devoid of merits, stand dismissed.
